evals.name: cargo-lock-investigation
evals.prompt: on a eu un souci relou cette semaine sur natalia — j'ai lancé plusieurs agents en parallèle sur apps/server et ils se bloquaient tous mutuellement au moment des tests. j'ai fini par comprendre que c'était cargo qui pose un lock sur target/. ça mériterait un article sur le blog, genre pourquoi paralléliser des agents sur du rust c'est pas si simple. tu peux me le rédiger ?
evals.expected_output: MDX article in apps/blog with inline sources on the cargo locking mechanism, no invented benchmark figures, a reliability callout stating what was verified against which cargo version and what was not.
assertions: Article saved as .mdx under apps/blog/src/content/posts/{locale}/
Frontmatter carries title, description, date and status
status is draft, not published
No import statement anywhere (MDX components are auto-imported)
MDX directive nesting uses increasing colon counts (card inside card-group, step inside step-group)
No section or callout is named after a methodology step or a coverage item
Claims that rot carry their version or date at the point of claim, not in a banner
Thin or missing evidence is disclosed in the prose, in the author's voice, where the claim sits
Factual claims carry inline source links at the claim, not a bundled list at the end
Every external link is a real specific URL, no placeholders or invented paths
Coverage: the prerequisites the reader needs are stated
Coverage: at least one serious counter-argument is presented, not a strawman
Coverage: the limits of what is claimed are stated
Coverage: what remains open, contested or unverified is named
Coverage: the article ends with an actionable next step
Headings are sentence case, not Title Case (humanizer pattern 16)
No emoji and no curly quotation marks (humanizer patterns 17 and 18)
The target-directory lock is sourced to cargo's own documentation or source, not a third-party blog post
No invented timing, duration or benchmark figure appears anywhere
No em dash outside quoted material
French register: que l'on throughout, never qu'on
The author's own work carries the article; external sources support rather than lead
